newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called slightly lower, cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called slightly lower, cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open marginally lower Monday despite early talk of steady cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.16 to $2.17 after settling higher Friday at $2.188 per million British thermal units.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub, La., were talked unchanged at $2.17-2.20 per mmBtu.
"If we can break through $2.16, we're looking for support at $2.12," one trader said.
The next backstop was pegged at $2.08. Resistance was seen at $2.25, and then at $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44.

Warmer-than-normal weather is expected to blanket the Northeast and upper Midwest throughout most of this week, while mostly seasonable levels are forecast elsewhere in the U.S. Temperatures in southern California are expected to reach highs in the mid-to-high 70s F, Weather Services Corp reported.
In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly to about $2.15. Midcon pipes were two to three cents higher around $2.05, while New York city gate gas prices were also up slightly to about $2.40.
